newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to replace jet fighters by year-end -agency.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to replace jet fighters by year-end -agency.

text.p: Taiwan's air force will complete installation of the first three wings of advanced fighter jets made in the United States, France and Taiwan by the end of this year, the state-run Central News Agency said on Saturday.

The agency quoted the island's air force commander-in-chief Huang Hsien-jung as saying that one wing each of U.S. F16s, French Mirage 2000-5s and Taiwan's own Indigenous Defence Fighters (IDFs) would replace aging planes by the end of 1997.
One wing in Taiwan has sixty planes.

Taiwan took delivery of its first F16 fighters from Lockheed Martin Corp in July 1996. The first delivery of Dassault Aviation's Mirage fighters was expected to arrive in Taiwan in May 1997, the agency said.

China, which has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war separated them in 1949, has pressured foreign powers not to sell advanced military equipment to Taipei and protested the F16 and Mirage deals.
Huang said with the new fighters Taiwan continues to stay ahead of the Chinese air force, despite Beijing's own efforts to upgrade with the purchase of new fighters like the Russian Sukhoi-27.
China has threatened to take the island back by force if it declares dependence.
Taiwan has ordered a total 150 F16 fighters and 60 Mirages and its IDF programme aims to build 130 fighters so 160 jets would remain to be activated.
